How high the land sits
How high the people sit

  • Dense lines along the border with Albania and Montenegro: the Accursed Mountains, with Gjeravica at 2,656 m.

  • Dukagjini in the west and the Kosovo Plain in the centre are flat, so the lines spread out. Most towns are here.

  • South of Prizren the rings bunch up tightest. These are the Sharr Mountains.

  • The lowest point, under 300 m, is where the White Drin crosses into Albania.

    Reading a real map

    Every line is one slice

    Cut a hill at even heights and look down from above. Each cut is one ring on the map.

    Watch the highlighted slice move up the hill.

    The bends tell the story

    The shape and spacing of the lines show the terrain.

    1. 1Ridge. Lines bulge outward and point downhill.
    2. 2Valley. Lines fold into V's that point uphill.
    3. 3Gully. A tight notch cut into the side of a slope.
    4. 4Flat. Lines far apart, or barely any at all.
    5. 5Steep. Lines squeezed close together.

    Data

    Elevation
    Open satellite terrain model, resampled to about 1 km
    Land cover
    Esri / Impact Observatory, 10 m, 2024, resampled to about 150 m
    Built-up area
    European Commission JRC, GHSL built-up surface R2023A, 100 m
    Roads
    © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Motorways down to local main roads

    How it's worked out

    Rivers
    Traced from the elevation data, not from a map. The split between the three seas is an estimate, based on where each drop leaves Kosovo
    Built-up
    Square kilometres of roofs and paved built area inside Kosovo
    First light
    The sun's angle at sunrise and the hills in its way, plus 4 minutes for every degree further west

    Borders, town positions and timings are approximate. Not for navigation.
